sentences.text: This creature belongs to the Dromaeosauridae family, a group of theropod dinosaurs known as dromaeosaurines.
The defining feature is a single tooth measuring 12 millimeters in length, which is flat on one side and possesses specific ridges.
Scientists propose that the second teeth in the upper jaw might have been adapted for grooming feathers.
The species name translates to 'abrading,' describing the worn texture of the fossilized tooth.
Edward Drinker Cope introduced this genus in 1876 during the fierce rivalry known as the Bone Wars.
Remains were found in the Judith River Formation of Montana, dating to the late Cretaceous era.
Experts disagree on whether this genus is separate from Saurornitholestes langstoni, as the original specimen is too incomplete to confirm.
